metadata.name: Webalyzer Core
metadata.description: Everything pack: SEO, Open Graph, JSON-LD, accessibility, and AI-agent navigability — one run scores site quality for humans and agents.

SEO-01.name: Single H1 Per Page
SEO-01.description: Each page must have exactly one H1 tag. Multiple H1s confuse AI agents and search engines about the primary topic. Zero H1s make the page untitled for agents.

fix.instruction: Ensure every page has exactly one <h1> tag describing the primary topic. If multiple H1s exist, downgrade extras to <h2>. If zero exist, add one at the top of <body>.
fix.codeSnippet: Primary Topic of This Page

SEO-02.name: Title Tag Presence and Length
SEO-02.description: Every page must have a <title> tag between 30 and 60 characters. Missing titles make pages untitled in search results and agent context. Too long gets truncated.

fix.instruction: Add a <title> tag inside <head> with 30-60 characters. Include primary keyword and brand name.

SEO-03.name: Meta Description Presence
SEO-03.description: Each page should have a meta description between 120 and 160 characters. While not a ranking factor, it controls search snippet text and agent summary context.

fix.instruction: Add a meta description summarizing the page content in 120-160 characters.
fix.codeSnippet: <meta name="description" content="This page covers backend engineering with NestJS, PostgreSQL, and scalable API design for high-traffic systems.">

examples.input: <meta name="description" content="A comprehensive guide to building scalable backends with NestJS and PostgreSQL for modern applications.">

SEO-04.name: Canonical Link Tag
SEO-04.description: Each page should have a canonical URL to prevent duplicate content issues. AI agents use canonicals to identify the authoritative version of content.

fix.instruction: Add a canonical link tag pointing to the preferred version of this URL.

AG-01.name: HTML Lang Attribute
AG-01.description: The <html> tag must have a lang attribute. AI agents use this to determine language for summarization, translation, and content processing. Missing lang causes agent misinterpretation.

fix.instruction: Add lang attribute to the <html> tag using ISO 639-1 language code.
fix.codeSnippet:
<html lang="en">
<!-- or lang="bn" for Bangla, lang="zh" for Chinese -->

OG-01.name: Open Graph Title
OG-01.description: og:title gives AI agents and social scrapers the canonical page title for cards and summaries. Missing it falls back to <title>, which may be truncated or wrong in agent context.

fix.instruction: Add an og:title meta tag with the page's share title (40-60 chars).

OG-02.name: Open Graph Description
OG-02.description: og:description supplies the summary text agents and social cards use. Without it, agents infer from page body, often producing weak or off-topic summaries.

fix.instruction: Add an og:description meta tag (120-200 chars) summarizing the page.
fix.codeSnippet: <meta property="og:description" content="Shop the durable, eco-friendly Widget with free shipping and a 2-year warranty.">

OG-03.name: Open Graph Image
OG-03.description: og:image is the visual agents and social platforms pull for cards. Missing it means no visual signal in agent summaries and zero share-preview CTR.

fix.instruction: Add an og:image meta tag pointing to a 1200x630 (or larger) share image URL.

OG-04.name: Open Graph Type
OG-04.description: og:type tells agents the semantic nature of the page (product, article, website). Agents use it to route the page into the correct understanding/extraction path.

fix.instruction: Add an og:type meta tag (e.g. 'product', 'article', 'website').

JSONLD-01.name: JSON-LD Structured Data Present
JSONLD-01.description: Structured data (schema.org JSON-LD) is the primary signal AI agents (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude) read to extract facts, products, and entities. A page with no JSON-LD is nearly invisible to agentic retrieval.

fix.instruction: Add a <script type="application/ld+json"> block with schema.org markup describing the page entity.

JSONLD-03.name: Organization Schema Validity
JSONLD-03.description: Organization schema tells agents who publishes the site, enabling entity linking and brand mentions in agent answers. name and logo are the minimum agents use.

fix.instruction: Add Organization JSON-LD with name (string) and logo (absolute URL).

AXS-01.name: Images Must Have Alt Attribute
AXS-01.description: Images without alt text are invisible to screen readers AND to AI agents that parse the accessibility tree. Agents use alt text to understand visual content; screen-reader users hear nothing.

fix.instruction: Add an alt attribute to every . Describe meaningful images; use alt="" (empty) for purely decorative images so assistive tech skips them.

AXS-02.name: Form Controls Have Accessible Names
AXS-02.description: Inputs, selects, and textareas need a programmatic name: an associated <label for>, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title. Without one, screen readers announce 'blank edit text' and AI agents cannot map fields when filling forms.

fix.instruction: Give each form control an id and an associated <label for> matching it — or an aria-label if a visible label is impractical.
fix.codeSnippet:
<label for="email">Email</label>
<input type="email" id="email" name="email">
<input type="search" aria-label="Search products">

AXS-03.name: Label For References Existing Elements
AXS-03.description: A <label for> pointing at a nonexistent id associates no control: the label is dead, the field stays unnamed. Broken pairs are common after refactors and block both assistive tech and agent form-filling.

fix.instruction: Either update label's for attribute to an existing id, or wrap the control inside the label and drop the for attribute.
fix.codeSnippet:
<label for="email">Email</label>
<input type="email" id="email"> <!-- ids must match -->

AXS-04.name: aria-labelledby References Exist
AXS-04.description: aria-labelledby contains space-separated id tokens; every token must resolve to an element. Dangling ids leave the accessible name broken — screen readers announce nothing and agents lose the label.

fix.instruction: Point every aria-labelledby token at an id that exists on the page, or remove the attribute.

AXS-05.name: aria-describedby References Exist
AXS-05.description: aria-describedby points at helper text by id. A dangling reference erases the description from the accessibility tree, hiding validation hints and instructions from both screen readers and agents.

fix.instruction: Point every aria-describedby token at an id that exists on the page, or remove the attribute.

AXS-06.name: No Positive Tabindex
AXS-06.description: tabindex values above 0 force a custom focus order that breaks keyboard and agent navigation predictably. Use 0 (natural order) or -1 (programmatically focusable only).

fix.instruction: Replace positive tabindex values with 0 (or -1 when the element should only be focused via script). Reorder the DOM if focus order must change.
fix.codeSnippet:
<div tabindex="0">   <!-- wrong -->
<div tabindex="-1">  <!-- ok, JS-focusable -->
<button>              <!-- ok, natural order -->

AXS-07.name: No Duplicate IDs
AXS-07.description: Duplicate id values make every id reference ambiguous: label[for], aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, and CSS/JS selectors resolve to the FIRST match only. Agents and assistive tech silently target the wrong element.

fix.instruction: Make every id unique. Search the reported values and rename repeats; update any label[for]/aria-* references that pointed at the old id.

AXS-08.name: Heading Hierarchy Has No Skips
AXS-08.description: Headings form the document outline agents use to segment content. Skipping levels (h2 followed by h4) breaks the outline for screen-reader navigation and weakens agent summarization structure.

fix.instruction: Increase heading levels by one at a time (h2 → h3, never h2 → h4). Use CSS to control visual size, not the heading tag choice.

AXS-09.name: Skip Navigation Link
AXS-09.description: A skip link lets keyboard and agent users jump past repeated navigation to the main content. Without it, every page forces re-traversing the full nav before reaching content.

fix.instruction: Add a skip link as the first focusable element in <body> pointing at your main content container id.
fix.codeSnippet:
Skip to main content
...
...

AXS-10.name: Main Landmark Present
AXS-10.description: A <main> landmark (or role="main") marks the primary content region. Screen readers offer landmark jumps to it, and agents use it to separate content from chrome when extracting page text.

fix.instruction: Wrap the page's primary content in a single <main id="main"> element (pair it with the skip link).

AXS-11.name: Navigation Landmark Present
AXS-11.description: A <nav> landmark (or role="navigation") labels the site's link clusters. Assistive tech lists it as a jump target and agents distinguish navigation links from content links by it.

fix.instruction: Wrap primary link clusters in <nav>. If multiple navs exist, label them with aria-label.

AXS-12.name: Links Have A Name
AXS-12.description: Empty links with no aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title announce as nothing in screen readers and give agents an anchor with no semantic identity. Every link must expose a discernible name.

fix.instruction: Give empty links visible text, an aria-label, or (for icon links) an accessible name via aria-label.
fix.codeSnippet: ... Cart (3)

AXS-13.name: Buttons Have A Name
AXS-13.description: Empty buttons with no accessible name announce as 'button' with no purpose. Screen-reader users and agent parsers cannot tell what activating the control does.

fix.instruction: Put text inside the button, or add aria-label describing the action (required for icon-only buttons).

AXS-14.name: Iframes Have Title
AXS-14.description: An iframe without a title attribute gives no indication of its content. Screen readers announce 'frame' with nothing else; agents cannot classify embedded content (maps, videos, widgets).

fix.instruction: Add a descriptive title attribute to every iframe describing what it embeds.

AXS-15.name: Valid Lang Format
AXS-15.description: The lang attribute must be a well-formed BCP 47 / ISO 639 tag (en, en-US, zh-Hans-CN). Malformed values make text-to-speech pick wrong pronunciation and agents misroute translation.

fix.instruction: Use a valid language tag: 2-3 letter language code, optionally followed by region/script subtags (en, en-US, pt-BR, zh-Hans-CN).

AXS-16.name: No Focusable Content Inside aria-hidden
AXS-16.description: aria-hidden="true" hides content from assistive tech, but focusable descendants remain tabbable — keyboard users land on invisible elements. Agents reading the accessibility tree and the DOM disagree about what exists.

fix.instruction: Either remove aria-hidden from containers holding interactive elements, or make those elements unfocusable (tabindex="-1") and remove them from the tab order.

AXS-17.name: Valid ARIA Role Values
AXS-17.description: role attributes must use tokens from the WAI-ARIA specification. A typo (rol="buton", custom roles) makes the element fall back to its native semantics — assistive tech and agents misclassify the control.

fix.instruction: Replace invalid role values with a token from the WAI-ARIA roles list — or remove the role and use the correct native element (e.g. <button> instead of <div role="button">).
fix.codeSnippet:
<div role="button">   <!-- typo: role="buton" breaks it -->
<button>              <!-- preferred -->

AXS-18.name: Viewport Must Not Disable Zoom
AXS-18.description: user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1 blocks pinch-zoom for low-vision users (WCAG 1.4.4 violation). Agents previewing mobile layouts treat forced zoom limits as a usability defect signal.

fix.instruction: Remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1 from the viewport meta tag.

AG-02.name: Clickable Components Expose Stable Hooks
AG-02.description: AI agents locate controls by stable selectors: id, name, or aria-label. Buttons and clickable inputs with none of these are addressable only by exact text, which breaks when copy changes or is localized.

fix.instruction: Give every clickable component a stable hook: an id (preferred), name, or aria-label. Agents and test automation then target it without depending on display text.

AG-03.name: llms.txt Present
AG-03.description: llms.txt is the emerging standard for giving AI agents a curated, token-efficient guide to a site's content and endpoints. Missing it forces agents to crawl blindly and summarize raw HTML.

fix.instruction: Publish an /llms.txt file at the site root: markdown with links to key pages, APIs, and docs, preceded by a one-line summary of the site.
fix.codeSnippet:
# Example Corp

> Example Corp builds developer tools for CI/CD pipelines.

## Docs
- [Getting started](https://example.com/docs/start): quickstart guide
- [API reference](https://example.com/docs/api): REST endpoints

AG-04.name: robots.txt Present
AG-04.description: robots.txt is the first file every crawler — search and AI alike — requests. A 404 means agents get no crawl guidance and may either over-crawl or assume the site is unfriendly to bots.

fix.instruction: Publish a /robots.txt allowing well-behaved crawlers and pointing to the sitemap.

AG-05.name: sitemap.xml Present
AG-05.description: The sitemap is how agents and search engines enumerate the site's URLs without crawling guesswork. Without it, deep pages may never be discovered by AI agents at all.

fix.instruction: Publish a /sitemap.xml listing every important URL, and reference it from robots.txt.

AG-06.name: No javascript: Links
AG-06.description: javascript: hrefs do nothing for non-executing clients. AI agents parsing raw HTML and users with scripting disabled get a dead link that pretends to navigate.

fix.instruction: Replace javascript: hrefs with real URLs where navigation is intended, or use a <button> with a click handler for in-page actions.
fix.codeSnippet: Settings

AG-07.name: No Dead Hash-Only Links
AG-07.description: href="#" is a placeholder handled by JavaScript events. Agents following links and no-JS users get sent to the top of the page instead of the intended destination.

fix.instruction: Point placeholder links at their real destination. If the link only triggers JS, make it a <button> instead of an <a>.

AG-08.name: Links Must Have href
AG-08.description: An <a> without href is not a link: it is excluded from the link graph agents crawl, announced without link semantics, and unreachable by keyboard.

fix.instruction: Add an href to every anchor, or replace it with a <button>/<span> if it is styled text rather than a link.

AG-09.name: Form Inputs Have name Attributes
AG-09.description: Form submission serializes fields by their name attribute. An input without name is silently dropped from the POST — agents and users can fill it, but the server never receives the value.

fix.instruction: Add a name attribute to every form input so its value is included in submission.

AG-10.name: WebSite JSON-LD Present
AG-10.description: WebSite schema identifies the site entity to AI assistants — its name and canonical URL anchor every answer that references the site. Missing it, agents describe the site from guesswork.

fix.instruction: Add WebSite JSON-LD on the homepage with name (string) and url (absolute).

AG-11.name: External Links Use rel noopener
AG-11.description: target="_blank" without rel="noopener" lets the opened page script-window.opener back into your origin — a tab-nabbing vector that security scanners and cautious agents flag.

fix.instruction: Add rel="noopener noreferrer" to every target="_blank" link.

AG-12.name: No Semantic-less Click Handlers
AG-12.description: div/span with onclick but no role or tabindex are invisible to the accessibility tree: screen readers skip them and agents cannot classify them as controls. Use native interactive elements.

fix.instruction: Replace div/span click handlers with <button> (or <a href> for navigation). If you must keep the element, add role and tabindex plus keyboard handlers.
